content: 1. Ahmed K and colleagues conducted a study on the use of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention among African women, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2012. The study evaluated the efficacy and safety of PrEP in this population. 2. McCormack S and Dunn D presented findings from the PROUD study, a pragmatic open-label randomized trial of PrEP, at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in Seattle, Washington, in 2015. 3. Grohskopf LA and colleagues performed a randomized trial to assess the clinical safety of daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate among HIV-uninfected men who have sex with men (MSM) in the United States. The results were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013. 4. Hosek SG and colleagues investigated the acceptability and feasibility of an HIV PrEP trial among young MSM. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013. 5. Molina JM and colleagues reported on the ANRS Ipergay trial, which evaluated on-demand PrEP with oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine (TDF-FTC) in MSM. The results were presented at CROI in Seattle, Washington, in 2015. 6. Kibengo FM and colleagues conducted a randomized clinical trial in Uganda to evaluate the safety, adherence, and acceptability of intermittent tenofovir/emtricitabine as PrEP among HIV-uninfected individuals in serodiscordant relationships. The study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 7. Mutua G and colleagues assessed the safety and adherence to intermittent PrEP for HIV-1 prevention among African MSM and female sex workers. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2012. 8. Roux S presented data from the HPTN 067/ADAPT Cape Town study, which compared daily and non-daily PrEP dosing in African women, at CROI in Seattle, Washington, in 2015. 9. Wilton J and colleagues reviewed the use of PrEP for managing sexually acquired HIV risk. Their review was published in HIV/AIDS (Auckland, NZ) in 2015. 10. Martin M and colleagues analyzed renal function among participants in the Bangkok Tenofovir Study, a trial conducted in Thailand from 2005 to 2012. The results were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014. 11. Solomon MM and colleagues examined changes in renal function associated with the use of oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for PrEP. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2014. 12. Kasonde M and colleagues studied changes in bone mineral density among HIV-uninfected young adults in Botswana participating in a randomized trial of PrEP with tenofovir-emtricitabine or placebo. The study was published in PLoS One in 2014. 13. Liu AY and colleagues investigated bone mineral density in HIV-negative men participating in a tenofovir PrEP randomized clinical trial in San Francisco. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2011. 14. Callahan R and colleagues explored pregnancy and contraceptive use among women participating in the FEM-PrEP trial. The results were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2015. 15. Murnane PM and colleagues demonstrated that PrEP for HIV-1 prevention does not reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraception in preventing pregnancy. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2014. 16. Mugo NR and colleagues analyzed pregnancy incidence and outcomes among women receiving PrEP for HIV prevention in a randomized clinical trial. The study was published in JAMA in 2014. 17. Liu A and colleagues examined sexual risk behavior among HIV-uninfected MSM participating in a tenofovir PrEP randomized trial in the United States. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013. 18. Grant RM and colleagues conducted the iPrEx study, which evaluated the efficacy of PrEP for HIV prevention in MSM. The results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2010. 19. Baeten JM and colleagues conducted the Partners PrEP study, which assessed antiretroviral prophylaxis for HIV prevention in heterosexual men and women. The findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2012. 20. Heffron R and colleagues demonstrated that PrEP is effective for HIV-1 prevention among women using depot medroxyprogesterone acetate for contraception. The study was published in AIDS in 2014. 21. Lehman DA and colleagues evaluated the risk of drug resistance among individuals acquiring HIV within a randomized clinical trial of singleor dual-agent PrEP. The findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2015. 22. Marrazzo JM and colleagues conducted the VOICE study, which assessed tenofovir-based PrEP for HIV prevention among African women. The results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015. 23. Peterson L and colleagues conducted a phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for HIV prevention in women. The study was published in PLoS Clinical Trials in 2007. 24. Guest G and colleagues analyzed changes in sexual risk behavior among participants in a PrEP HIV prevention trial. The findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2008. 25. The CHER trial demonstrated a significant reduction in mortality among infants who initiated ART immediately compared to those who deferred ART based on CD4 percentage. The results were published in 2014. 26. The PREDICT trial, conducted in Cambodia and Thailand, showed no difference in outcomes for children aged 1-12 years with CD4 percentages of 15-24% who initiated ART immediately versus deferred ART.
